question.text: The intermolecular potential energy for the moleculesA ,B , C and D given below suggests that:

options.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></math> has the shortest bond length
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> has the largest bond enthalpy
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></math> is more electronegative than other atoms.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> has the stiffest bond.

solution.text: Bond enthalpy of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>AB</mi></math> bond is highest so <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> bond is more strong and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> is highest electronegative atom.
